summary.oneLiner: Vadodara-based container-glass manufacturer supplying flint and, from FY2025-26, coloured (amber/green) glass bottles to the alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverage, food, pharmaceutical, personal-care and homecare industries in India and overseas.
summary.business: Haldyn Glass Limited manufactures glass containers for packaging, operating in a single primary business segment viz. glass bottles / containers. It historically made predominantly flint (transparent) containers and during FY 2025-26 also commenced manufacture of coloured (amber/brown and green) glass bottles for the beer segment. Liquor continues to account for the largest share of the Company's offtake, but the portfolio now spans liquor, food & beverages, pharmaceuticals, softdrinks and toiletries, sold to customers in India and in international markets including the US.

currentContext.strengths: Established presence and long-standing customer relationships in the US market, which allowed the Company to keep servicing US obligations through the FY26 tariff disruption|Investments made over several years in plant modernisation and state-of-the-art inspection technology, which management says are now translating into a meaningfully diversified customer base and access to more profitable segments|Technical capability to make beer bottles - high precision, stringent quality/food-safety audits, and lightweight yet structurally robust containers able to withstand pressurised filling and returnable use|Product-mix diversification across liquor, food & beverages, pharmaceuticals, softdrinks and toiletries, reducing significant dependence on any single segment|Supply-chain resilience: management states it continued manufacturing without significant curtailment during the FY26 energy/freight/soda-ash disruption when some glass makers globally and in India curtailed or suspended production|56.80% jointly controlled interest in Haldyn Heinz Fine Glass Private Limited and a wholly-owned US subsidiary, Haldyn Glass USA Inc., supporting the international franchise
currentContext.strategies: Drive growth through sustainability initiatives and diversify into high margin product segments, with financial prudence, operational efficiency and sustainable business practices as the stated foundation|Enter and scale the coloured beer-bottle segment - a decision backed by market research that identified a demand-supply gap in quality glass beer bottles in India - after enhancing manufacturing capability for high-precision, lightweight, pressure-resistant returnable containers|Broaden the product basket beyond flint containers so the portfolio spans liquor, food & beverages, pharmaceuticals, softdrinks and toiletries, reducing significant dependence on any single segment|Keep diversifying the customer base in Indian and international markets and address more profitable segments, on the back of past investments in plant modernisation, state-of-the-art inspection technology and skills/capability enhancement|Defend and grow the US franchise - continue servicing US business obligations through tariff volatility and actively pursue new opportunities that require a long lead time to fructify|Manage input-cost and logistics exposure proactively - timely procurement of critical raw materials, effective energy management and agile operational responses - to avoid production curtailment|The Company pays a regular equity dividend and retains the rest in the business: for FY 2025-26 the Board recommended a dividend of 70%, i.e. Rs 0.70 per equity share of Rs 1 face value, for member approval at the 35th AGM, payable during FY 2026-27, and the directors do not propose to transfer any amount to reserves for the year. No securities were issued or allotted during the year, and the paid-up capital was unchanged against an authorised capital of Rs 1,500 lakhs. Employee alignment is run through two ongoing Employee Stock Appreciation Rights Plans (ESAR Plan 2021 and ESAR Plan 2024, the latter approved at the 33rd AGM) administered by the Nomination and Remuneration Committee, under which ESARs were granted to identified employees during the year with no new plan introduced. Unclaimed dividends and the related shares are transferred to the IEPF as required. The stated financial philosophy in the MD&A is one of 'maintaining financial prudence, operational efficiency, and sustainable business practices'. No buyback, debt-reduction target, credit rating or formal dividend-distribution policy appears in the routed sections.
currentContext.expansion: The only expansion the FY 2025-26 annual report describes is the entry into coloured glass: having earlier made predominantly flint (transparent) containers, the Company commenced manufacturing coloured (amber/brown and green) glass bottles for the beer segment during the year and commercialised them within FY26. Management frames this as backed by market research that identified a demand-supply gap in quality glass beer bottles in India, and says it required enhanced manufacturing capability for high-precision, lightweight yet structurally robust containers able to withstand pressurised filling and returnable use, plus stringent quality audits and food-safety standards; it credits its enhanced infrastructure and technical expertise, built through several years of investment in plant modernisation, state-of-the-art inspection technology and skills/capability enhancement. No new plant, furnace, line, capacity addition, commissioning date or ramp timeline is disclosed anywhere in the routed sections, and the report gives no capacity table. The accounts do carry a capital-commitments disclosure (estimated amount of contracts remaining to be executed on capital account, at both standalone page 111 and consolidated page 187), but the routed block for it arrived without a unit line and without dated period headers, so the figures could not be carried into capex_disclosed.

risks.risk: Energy and fuel cost volatility in an energy-intensive process
risks.note: Management states the glass industry is energy intensive and heavily dependent on stable logistics and raw-material supply chains, and was particularly vulnerable to the FY26 disruptions; higher energy prices from supply disruptions and the new armed conflict that emerged in March 2026 are named as near-term risks to input-cost stability. Several glass manufacturers globally and some within India were compelled to curtail or temporarily suspend production.

risks.risk: Raw-material (soda ash) price volatility and supply-chain disruption
risks.note: Price volatility in fuel and soda ash, freight disruptions and logistical constraints are explicitly listed among the challenges management had to address in advance to avoid curtailment; continuity depends on timely procurement of critical raw materials.

Management says competitive pressure due to the current surplus capacity in segments of the domestic glass industry will continue to pose challenges - a structural pricing risk for a single-segment container-glass producer.
Explicitly flagged in Risks and Concerns; the Company sells into international markets including the US and imports/ships inputs, so both translation and freight exposure sit on the margin.

risks.risk: Trade-policy and tariff risk on exports
risks.note: US reciprocal tariffs, initially set at 26% for Indian goods and subsequently revised higher from August 2025, adversely affected Indian glass and packaging exports; management cites lingering impact of US tariff escalations and persistent uncertainty around trade-policy normalisation, though it also notes tariffs on Chinese glass have opened an opportunity.

Liquor continues to account for the largest share of the Company's offtake and the business falls within a single primary segment (glass bottles / containers), so demand or regulatory shocks in alcobev pass through directly; diversification into beer, food, pharma, softdrinks and toiletries is the stated mitigation.

risks.risk: Product substitution and bottle reuse in low-value brands
risks.note: The MD&A's own market view notes the India glass packaging market grows at only ~4.3% CAGR through 2030 'inspite of reuse of bottles by customers and substitution by other packing alternatives in low value brands' - a structural volume drag.

risks.risk: Technology obsolescence, talent retention and execution risk on expansion
risks.note: The Board's risk-management disclosure names the common risks inter alia as regulatory risk, competition, financial risk, technology obsolescence, human resources risk, political risks, investments, retention of talent, expansion of facilities and product price risk, managed under a Risk Management Policy.
